indexes._comment: Community feed: live posts, newest first (docs/03 §9 reverse-chron).
Founder review queue: unreviewed flags, oldest first.

Ember's long-term memory. `findNearest` requires an explicit VECTOR index — without it every recall throws FAILED_PRECONDITION at runtime, and the coach silently loses its memory while still answering. Dimension must match EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS in lib/memories.ts.

fieldOverrides._comment: Feed replies arrive in one collection-group query instead of one per post. A single-field index needs COLLECTION_GROUP scope declared explicitly; the automatic ones are collection-scoped only.
One collection-group query for a viewer's own reactions, instead of a read per post.

deleteUserData finds every report a departing account made in one collection-group query. The uid is also the document ID, but a collection-group filter on documentId() needs a full resource path, so the id alone is not queryable - hence the field, and hence this override. Without the COLLECTION_GROUP scope the query throws FAILED_PRECONDITION at runtime and erasure silently leaves the uid under every post they reported. The emulator does not enforce indexes, so this only ever fails in production.

pruneDevices sweeps stale push registrations across every user in one collection-group query rather than paging the whole userbase. Without the COLLECTION_GROUP scope here the query throws FAILED_PRECONDITION at runtime and the cron quietly prunes nothing.

Thread-notification rows are swept by the pruneDevices cron with a collection-group query on lastReplyAtMs. Without the COLLECTION_GROUP scope declared here that query throws FAILED_PRECONDITION at runtime and the sweep silently prunes nothing - the same trap devices.lastSeenAt above exists to document.

The inbox is read by the app newest-first and swept by the pruneDevices cron oldest-first, so this field needs THREE index configs and every one of them is load-bearing. COLLECTION+DESCENDING is the app's own query (FirebaseNotificationsRepository.watch, orderBy createdAtMs descending); COLLECTION_GROUP+ASCENDING is pruneOldNotifications. A field override REPLACES Firestore's automatic single-field indexes rather than adding to them, so declaring only the two ascending ones DELETED the descending index the app depends on - and the app's failure was invisible, because NotificationsStore treats a stream error as an empty inbox. The inbox rendered its empty state and the bell showed no badge for every user, while the rules, the send path and the cron all stayed green. Adding a scope here is never additive: list every config the field is queried with.
